summary.oneLiner: Oberoi Realty is capitalizing on acute supply constraints in Mumbai's premium residential market with high-margin, ready-to-move-in projects like Worli's 360 West, while strategically advancing commercial and redevelopment pipelines that offer multi-year growth visibility and pricing power amid rising input costs.
summary.business: Oberoi Realty Limited develops residential, commercial, hospitality, retail and social infrastructure projects, concentrated in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (Goregaon, Mulund, Borivali, Thane, Worli). It also operates a hospitality business, and owns and leases investment-grade office and retail properties for rental income, giving it a mix of development sales and recurring lease/rental cash flows.

Real Estate Development: Residential apartments (Elysian, Eternia, Enigma, Sky City Residential, Forestville, Jardin, Three Sixty West)
Commercial office space (Commerz, Commerz II, Commerz III, International Business Park)
Retail malls (Oberoi Mall, Sky City Mall)
Hospitality: The Westin Mumbai Garden City hotel

endMarkets: Mumbai Metropolitan Region (western suburbs, central suburbs, Thane) — 100% of operations are domestic; company does not export and has no international projects or offices

currentContext.strengths: Brand reputation with higher recall that influences buying decisions and supports premium realizations|Track record of quality project execution with contemporary architecture|Continuous cash flows from investment/development properties, providing stability through adverse business cycles|Conservative debt practice combined with a strong cash balance, giving significant leveraging headroom for expansion|Outsourcing model using globally renowned architects/contractors, enabling scalability and contemporary design/construction quality|Strong corporate governance culture with transparency and high business ethics|Experienced, highly qualified design and project-management execution team
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the development pipeline through strategic business development initiatives and acquisition of new land parcels|Expand retail footprint through development of new retail destinations across strategic locations|Expand presence in key markets while strengthening the portfolio across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality segments|Grow development potential through a balanced mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region|Company pays dividends via quarterly interim payouts rather than a single final dividend; four interim dividends of Rs. 2 per equity share each (Rs. 8 aggregate) were declared for FY2025-26 and put to shareholders at the AGM to be confirmed as the final dividend for the year. It complies with the statutory requirement to transfer dividends and shares unclaimed for 7 consecutive years to the Investor Education Protection Fund (IEPF).
currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company launched Elysian Tower D at Oberoi Garden City, Goregaon East and Tower H at the Sky City project in Borivali East. Sky City (Borivali East, ~25 acre parcel, estimated total carpet area of about 4.5 million sq.ft.) received occupancy certificates for Tower A to E. Forestville at Kolshet, Thane is an under-development ~18 acre parcel with an estimated total carpet area of about 1.8 million sq.ft. Jardin, at Oberoi Garden City Thane (Pokhran Road-2), is an under-development ~75 acre parcel. Three Sixty West, Worli, a mixed-use residential development of 2 high-rise towers, was developed through a joint-venture entity; the Company retired as a member of that unincorporated association on March 3, 2023 and currently owns apartments in the project. On the business-development front, the Company added close to 4 million square feet of development potential during the year across key micro-markets in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, through a mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships, strengthening its future development pipeline.
currentContext.mdna: Real estate sector benefiting from structural trends of rising urbanization, increasing disposable incomes and evolving consumer preferences|Residential demand remains strong, especially in mid-income and premium segments, supported by stable interest rates and renewed buyer confidence|Commercial real estate witnessing gradual recovery driven by demand for high-quality office space and growth in IT, BFSI and startup sectors|Mumbai residential demand supported by a continued shift from rental to ownership housing and homebuyers prioritizing larger living spaces and improved amenities|Grade A office leasing across metro cities strengthening, led by demand from global capability centres and domestic corporates and a shift toward world-class, sustainable infrastructure; Company's Commercial Offices at International Business Park operating at a record occupancy level of ~91%|Retail demand for premium destinations continues to outmatch supply of spaces aligned with evolving occupier expectations; Retail Portfolio strengthening with addition of leading global brands across technology, entertainment, fashion and dining|Infrastructure development (metro rail expansion, coastal road, trans-harbour connectivity) expected to be a key catalyst unlocking new growth corridors and positively impacting property values|India's expanding affluent consumer base and growing billionaire population driving demand for premium, design-led and future-ready developments, with structural premiumisation favouring luxury and upper-tier residential segments|Company added close to 4 million square feet of development potential during the year across key micro-markets in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, through a mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships

risks.note: Management flags unanticipated delays in obtaining regulatory/project approvals as a challenge to executing its development pipeline on schedule.
Availability of an accomplished and trained labour force is flagged as a constraint on project execution.
Increased cost of manpower is cited as a cost pressure on project execution and margins.
Rising cost of construction, led by increases in commodity prices, is flagged as pressuring development economics.
Company flags the pace of growth in auxiliary infrastructure facilities (roads, utilities, connectivity around project sites) as a factor affecting its developments.
Management flags an over-regulated environment as a structural challenge to the real estate business.

one-line thesis: Oberoi Realty is capitalizing on acute supply constraints in Mumbai's premium residential market with high-margin, ready-to-move-in projects like Worli's 360 West, while strategically advancing commercial and redevelopment pipelines that offer multi-year growth visibility and pricing power amid rising input costs.
financial scorecard: rev: +45% YoY; EBITDA: +52% YoY; PAT: +68% YoY; orderbook: ₹12,500 Cr; netdebt: ₹1,800 Cr (net cash positive)
guidance: Launches planned in Thane, Borivali, and Goregaon within Q3FY23; Glaxo land use decision (residential vs. commercial) expected by end of Q3FY23; no formal guidance issued beyond near-term launches.
order book & pipeline: ₹12,500 Cr (including ₹8,500 Cr from Worli 360 West unsold inventory and ₹4,000 Cr from other projects)
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: 360 West (Worli) sold 77/200 units at ₹1.0-1.1 Cr/sq.ft RERA carpet; Goregaon/Borivali sold out Towers A/B; Mulund pricing up 5-10%; Retail: Borivali Mall pre-COVID consumption restored; Commercial: Commerz III nearing completion with strong tenant interest; Redevelopment: SRA site adjacent to Sky City cleared, 95% vacated.
growth verticals / optionality: Glaxo land parcel (10+ acres) for commercial/mall or residential; redevelopment pipeline in Mumbai (multiple projects in advanced talks); potential for 1M sq.ft commercial expansion in Borivali/Sky City corridor; expansion beyond MMR under evaluation.
margins & cost dynamics: Residential margins expanding due to pricing power (Worli realization up 50% YoY); input costs up 15-20% (labor, materials, approvals); 5-10% price hikes implemented across projects since Oct 2022; commercial margins expected to be 35%+ post-completion.
capex / expansion: Total capex H1FY23: ₹913 Cr; Commerz III: ₹400 Cr pending; Borivali Mall: ₹400 Cr pending; Thane/Borivali launches: ₹300 Cr estimated; redevelopment: ₹200 Cr estimated; total FY23 capex guidance: ₹2,000 Cr.
capital allocation: Prioritizing project launches and capex for high-return assets (Worli, Commerz III, Thane); no dividends paid; debt reduction secondary to growth; land acquisition via redevelopment and TDRs to minimize cash outflow.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in Thane (Eco-Sensitive Zone reinstatement risk); interest rate volatility impacting buyer affordability; delays in redevelopment approvals; oversupply risk in non-premium segments; execution risk on large commercial projects.
management quality / tone: Confident, bullish, and proactive; management emphasizes pricing power, supply scarcity, and execution discipline; avoids overpromising on timelines but signals strong momentum; tone reflects control over narrative and market position.
non-obvious takeaways: Buyers are purchasing 2-3 units to create 12,000-15,000 sq.ft duplexes — indicating ultra-high-net-worth demand and asset consolidation behavior, not just housing needs; SRA redevelopment success without intermediaries is a rare competitive moat in Mumbai.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
